controls.title: Audit logs are implemented to support detection of anomalies and suspicious activity
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the logging is correctly scoped to the cardholder data environment, that all required event types are captured, or that detection of anomalies was timely.
controls.what_we_prove: Audit log events emitted by the in-scope cardholder data environment to the chain are stored with tamper-evident ordering, signed timestamps, and cryptographic anchoring.

controls.title: Audit logs capture required event types
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That every required event type was wired for emission. The chain receives what is sent; coverage configuration is the entity's responsibility.
controls.what_we_prove: Events of all submitted types are preserved in the chain with their original content intact and ordering stable. An assessor can verify which event types are reaching the chain.

controls.title: Audit logs are protected from destruction and unauthorized modifications
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That logs were protected during transmission from emitter to the chain. From the point of inclusion forward, integrity is enforced.
controls.what_we_prove: Once a log entry enters the chain, destruction or modification produces a mathematically detectable break. The protection is enforced cryptographically, not by access control alone.

controls.title: Audit log reviews are performed at the defined frequency (daily for specified event categories under v4.0)
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the review was substantive or that all events were actually examined. Under v4.0's targeted-risk-analysis allowance for non-critical assets (10.4.2), frequency for broader scope may be entity-determined; the chain records the review activity as performed.
controls.what_we_prove: Review events (who reviewed, when, what time range was covered) submitted to the chain are stored with stable ordering and signed timestamps. An assessor can confirm review activity actually happened on the dates claimed.

controls.title: Audit log history is retained and available for analysis
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the entity's retention configuration itself meets the PCI v4.0 Req 10.5.1 minimum (at least 12 months total with at least the most recent 3 months immediately available for analysis). Aleutian provides the durable substrate; meeting the duration target is the entity's configuration.
controls.what_we_prove: Chain entries are retained for the contracted retention period (default 7 years prod), accessible for assessor analysis, with verifiable integrity throughout.

controls.title: Security incident response includes alerts from security monitoring systems
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the response was timely or adequate. The chain records the response activity; the adequacy is the incident-response team's domain.
controls.what_we_prove: Incident-response events (alert receipt, triage, action, closure) submitted to the chain are stored with tamper-evident ordering and signed timestamps.

controls.title: Failures of critical security control systems are detected, alerted, and addressed promptly
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That critical security control systems are correctly identified and instrumented for failure detection in the first place. This control is marked designed (not operating) because automatic failure detection across the entity's systems is not yet a turnkey Aleutian capability — only the recording substrate is.
controls.what_we_prove: When critical-control-system failure events are emitted to the chain (alongside detection and remediation events), the chain stores them with tamper-evident ordering. The design supports failure-recording, not failure-detection.

controls_out_of_scope.reason: network security controls (firewalls, segmentation) are network-architecture
protect stored account data (encryption at rest, masking) is data-handling
protect cardholder data in transit is transport-layer
restrict access by need-to-know is access-control policy
identify users and authenticate access is identity-system
test security of systems and networks (penetration testing, IDS, change detection) is assurance activity
information security program management is organizational (12.10.5 incident response above is the relevant chain-evidenced subset)
